definitions.definition: A legal process that ends a marriage or domestic partnership. After a divorce is final, the parties are no longer married or in the domestic partnership.
A court process in which the parties remain legally married, but the court can divide property and debts and make orders concerning support and, when applicable, children.
A court determination that a marriage or domestic partnership was not legally valid from the start.
The date of the complete and final break in the marriage, shown by one spouse's intent to end the marriage and actions consistent with that intent.
The formal delivery of filed court papers to the other spouse or partner. In the ordinary divorce-start process, the filing party cannot personally serve the papers.

laws.title: California divorce residency requirement
laws.statement: For the ordinary California divorce process, one spouse generally must have lived in California for the preceding 6 months and in the county where the case is filed for the preceding 3 months. Different rules can apply to California-registered domestic partnerships and certain same-sex marriages.

laws.title: Divorce does not require the other spouse's agreement
laws.statement: California Courts states that a spouse does not need the other spouse's agreement to obtain a divorce.

laws.title: Minimum time before divorce can be final
laws.statement: A California divorce takes at least 6 months to become final. In the ordinary process, the waiting period is measured from service of the divorce papers or the other spouse's court response.

laws.title: Legal separation does not end the marriage
laws.statement: A legal separation leaves the parties legally married. It can address property, debts, financial support, and orders concerning children, and it does not have the same 6-month waiting period as divorce.

laws.title: Annulment requires a legal basis
laws.statement: A judge can annul a marriage only when there is a legally recognized reason that the marriage was invalid from the start. Agreement between the spouses by itself is not enough.

laws.title: Annulment may limit property division and spousal support
laws.statement: In an annulment, the court cannot always divide property and debts or order spousal support. These remedies can depend on whether a party qualifies as a putative spouse.

laws.title: Date of separation affects financial issues
laws.statement: The date of separation can affect characterization of property and debt and can affect spousal-support issues, including the length of the marriage considered by the court.

procedures.title: Standard California divorce process
procedures.description: California Courts organizes the ordinary divorce process into four main stages.
steps: Start the divorce case and notify the other spouse.
Exchange required financial information.
Resolve decisions concerning property, debts, children, and support by agreement or court process.
Submit the final paperwork so the divorce can become final.

procedures.title: Start a standard divorce or legal separation case
procedures.description: The ordinary process begins by filing the required court forms and formally serving the other spouse or partner.
steps: Confirm that the applicable filing requirements are met.
Complete the required starting forms, generally including FL-100 and FL-110.
File the forms with the court and pay the filing fee or request a fee waiver.
Have another qualified adult serve the filed papers on the other spouse or partner.
Complete the required proof of service process.

procedures.title: Use legal separation when divorce residency requirements are not yet met
procedures.description: Legal separation is an available route for a spouse who does not yet satisfy the ordinary divorce residency requirements.
steps: File for legal separation if its filing requirements are met.
Proceed using the legal-separation process.
After the divorce residency requirements are met, the petition may be amended to request divorce.

procedures.title: Start an annulment case
procedures.description: An annulment starts with filing court forms and serving the other spouse, but the requesting party must ultimately establish a legally recognized basis for annulment.
steps: Determine where the annulment case may be filed.
Complete and file FL-100 and FL-110.
Have the papers served on the other spouse by another adult.
File the proof of service.
Allow the response period to run.
Obtain the required court date or next-step instructions and present the legal basis for annulment to the judge.

procedures.title: Joint petition for divorce or legal separation
procedures.description: Beginning January 1, 2026, California permits spouses or partners using the joint-petition process to start a divorce or legal separation together. The joint petition starts the case but does not finish it.
steps: Both parties sign and file the joint-petition forms.
Exchange required financial disclosures.
Reach a written agreement resolving all issues.
Prepare and file the judgment and other required final paperwork.
Complete the remaining requirements and, for divorce, the applicable waiting period.
